name: Rainforest Alliance
mission: The Rainforest Alliance works to encourage better on-the-ground forestry practices by rewarding businesses, communities and governments that meet standards for sustainability.
theoryOfChange: Roughly 1.6 billion people around the world directly depend on forests for their livelihoods. Workers all over the world support their families with income earned from activities—like forestry, farming and tourism—that take place in rainforests, and many of them earn less than USD $1.25 a day.The economic security and well-being of farming and forest communities are central to our long-term vision of a rebalanced Earth. That's why we've embedded concrete strategies to support the environmental, economic, and social health of rural communities around the world into our training and certification programs.

strengths_deep_dive: In FY2024, the Rainforest Alliance achieved a high program expense ratio of <cite id="1">84.3%</cite>. This performance exceeds the 75% standard benchmark for nonprofit spending efficiency. Financial sustainability remains robust with working capital reserves sufficient for 7.8 months of operational continuity. The charity maintains high standards of public openness, supported by <cite id="5">a perfect 100 Accountability score on Charity Navigator</cite> and <cite id="4">a Platinum Seal from Candid</cite>.
rich_narrative.summary: The Rainforest Alliance protects global forests and rural livelihoods by helping businesses, farmers, and communities adopt sustainable agricultural and forestry practices. In FY2024, the organization managed <cite id="1">Total Revenue of $100,221,940</cite> while executing international grantmaking and sustainability certification programs. The organization maintains <cite id="5">a 91/100 overall score from Charity Navigator</cite>, reflecting strong accountability and organizational health. Financial records show that <cite id="1">84.3% of expenses went toward program services</cite>, well above the 75% sector benchmark. Operates in regions including West Africa, Latin America, and Southeast Asia, working with over ten million beneficiaries. Donations to the organization qualify as Sadaqah giving.
